Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Krishna clarifies that although He is unborn and His transcendental form never deteriorates, He appears in the material world through His internal potency while remaining fully transcendental.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Understanding how the unborn Divine manifests within physical reality without being bound by material laws.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna explains His divine nature: 'ajo 'pi sann avyayatma bhutanam isvaro 'pi san... sambhavamy atma-mayaya' (Although unborn and imperishable, I manifest by My own divine energy).
Outcome/Resolution: Establishes that divine appearance is an act of sovereign grace, unconditioned by material birth and decay.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Transcending Circumstantial Limits: Remaining untouched by external stress and physical constraints
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Core Unchanging Nature: Maintaining a stable identity despite changing external situations
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Autonomy Over Environment: Operating with agency rather than being controlled by outer events

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Ajo 'pi sann avyayatma (Unborn and imperishable in essence)
Atma-mayaya / Prakrtim svam adhisthaya (Manifesting through internal divine energy)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna explains that He remains unborn and transcendental, entering the material realm by His own creative power (atma-maya) without being subject to material decay or illusion.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Recognizing that your core consciousness remains intact despite external life changes fosters emotional resilience and identity stability.
